target_raw: Mozilla Crash Reports (crash dump stack traces, Jan-Nov 2017)

target_raw: CWE weakness classification scheme (MITRE)

target_canonical: Shin et al. complexity/churn/developer metrics for vulnerability prediction
target_raw: Shin et al. complexity/churn/developer metrics for vulnerability prediction

target_canonical: Theisen et al. crash-stack-trace attack surface approximation (crash features)
target_raw: Theisen et al. crash-stack-trace attack surface approximation (crash features)
evidence: Crash features: followed by the work of Theisen et al. [8], the crash features measure the number of time each source code file has crashed.

target_canonical: Theisen et al. crash-ranking unsupervised approach ('Crash' treatment)
target_raw: Theisen et al. crash-ranking unsupervised approach ('Crash' treatment)

target_canonical: Theisen et al. Firefox crash-history measurement (15.8% crashed files hold 73.6% vulns)
target_raw: Theisen et al. Firefox crash-history measurement (15.8% crashed files hold 73.6% vulns)
evidence: 15.8% of the "crashed" source code files in Mozilla Firefox contain 73.6% of known vulnerabilities [29].
ref: [29] C. Theisen, K. Herzig, B. Murphy, and L. Williams, "Risk-based attack surface approximation: how much data is enough?" ICSE-SEIP 2017, pp. 273-282.

target_canonical: Hatton code-inspection error rate (47% false negatives)
target_raw: Hatton code-inspection error rate (47% false negatives)
evidence: Hatton [11]'s report suggested that each "vulnerable" file has in average 47% chance of being mislabeled as "non-vulnerable" ... Following this report, we simulate
ref: [11] L. Hatton, "Testing the value of checklists in code inspections," IEEE Software, vol. 25, no. 4, 2008.

target_raw: Two-person inspection (Hatton) as error-correction baseline
evidence: Two-persons [11] check each label. In Step 3, if one file is labeled as "non-vulnerable" and has been reviewed by only one reviewer, it goes back into the queue
ref: [11] L. Hatton, "Testing the value of checklists in code inspections," IEEE Software, vol. 25, no. 4, 2008.

target_raw: Cormack'17 error correction for TAR (Cormack & Grossman)
evidence: Cormack'17 [31]: This is an advanced error correction method for citation screening. We reproduce half of Cormack'17 to correct false negatives only
ref: [31] G. V. Cormack and M. R. Grossman, "Navigating imprecision in relevance assessments on the road to total recall: Roger and me," SIGIR 2017, pp. 5-14.

target_raw: Knee/inflection-point stopping rule (Cormack & Grossman)
evidence: If slope<i/slope>i is greater than a specific threshold rho = 6, the review should be stopped. For details about this stopping rule, please refer to Cormack and Grossman [32].
ref: [32] G. V. Cormack and M. R. Grossman, "Engineering quality and reliability in technology-assisted review," pp. 75-84, 2016.

target_raw: Presumptive non-relevant examples (Cormack & Grossman)
evidence: Presumptive non-relevant examples is a technique created by Cormack and Grossman [34] to alleviate the sampling bias of negative (non-vulnerable) training data.
ref: [34] G. V. Cormack and M. R. Grossman, "Autonomy and reliability of continuous active learning for technology-assisted review," arXiv:1504.06868, 2015.

target_raw: Certainty sampling / continuous active learning protocol (Cormack & Grossman)
evidence: Cormack et al. [35], [43] use certainty sampling from beginning to end. Followed by our previous design for literature review [13], HARMLESS applies uncertainty sampling early on and certainty sampling afterward.
ref: [35] G. V. Cormack and M. R. Grossman, "Evaluation of machine-learning protocols for technology-assisted review in electronic discovery," SIGIR 2014, pp. 153-162.

target_canonical: Aggressive undersampling and uncertainty sampling (Wallace et al. patient active learning)
target_raw: Aggressive undersampling and uncertainty sampling (Wallace et al. patient active learning)
evidence: Aggressive undersampling is a data balancing technique first created by Wallace et al. [37]. During the training process, aggressive undersampling throws away majority
ref: [37] B. C. Wallace, T. A. Trikalinos, J. Lau, C. Brodley, and C. H. Schmid, "Semi-automated screening of biomedical citations for systematic reviews," BMC Bioinformatics, vol. 11, 2010.

target_canonical: Uniform random sampling recall estimator (Wallace et al.)
target_raw: Uniform random sampling recall estimator (Wallace et al.)
evidence: Uniform random sampling is applied as a baseline estimation. ... It was believed to be the most accurate estimation method before the introduction of SEMI [41].
ref: [41] B. C. Wallace, I. J. Dahabreh, K. H. Moran, C. E. Brodley, and T. A. Trikalinos, "Active literature discovery for scoping evidence reviews: How many needles are there," KDD-DMH 2013.

target_raw: Class-balanced SVM weighting and certainty sampling (Miwa et al.)
evidence: penalty is set to be "balanced" (balancing the penalty of misclassifying a training data point by the population of its class ...) as suggested by Miwa et al. [43].
ref: [43] M. Miwa, J. Thomas, A. O'Mara-Eves, and S. Ananiadou, "Reducing systematic review workload through certainty-based screening," J. Biomedical Informatics, vol. 51, pp. 242-253, 2014.

target_raw: scikit-learn SVC (soft-margin linear SVM)
evidence: The soft-margin linear SVM is implemented with the SVC package from scikit-learn. Default parameters are applied while kernel is set to be "linear"
ref: footnote 8: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.svm.SVC.html

target_raw: QN-S3VM semi-supervised SVM package (Gieseke et al.)
evidence: we test the S3VM learner implemented with the package from Gieseke et al. [49], [25].
ref: [49] F. Gieseke, A. Airola, T. Pahikkala, and O. Kramer, "Sparse quasi-newton optimization for semi-supervised support vector machines," ICPRAM 2012, pp. 45-54. (also [25])

target_raw: Total recall problem definition (TREC Total Recall track, Grossman & Cormack)
evidence: The target of total recall is to optimize the cost for achieving very high recall (ideally, very close to 100%) with a human assessor in the loop [12].
ref: [12] M. R. Grossman, G. V. Cormack, and A. Roegiest, "Trec 2016 total recall track overview," in TREC, 2016.

target_canonical: Walden et al. cross-project / text-vs-metrics vulnerability prediction results
target_raw: Walden et al. cross-project / text-vs-metrics vulnerability prediction results
evidence: cross-project prediction performances were generally poor—49%, 36% of the source code files need to be reviewed for finding 66%, 70% of the vulnerabilities
ref: [10] J. Walden, J. Stuckman, and R. Scandariato, "Predicting vulnerable components: Software metrics vs text mining," ISSRE 2014, pp. 23-33.

target_canonical: Scandariato et al. text-mining vulnerability prediction
target_raw: Scandariato et al. text-mining vulnerability prediction

ref: [5] R. Scandariato, J. Walden, A. Hovsepyan, and W. Joosen, "Predicting vulnerable software components via text mining," IEEE TSE, vol. 40, no. 10, pp. 993-1006, 2014.

target_raw: Meng et al. semi-supervised (label propagation) buffer-overflow prediction

target_raw: Microsoft nine-step ML pipeline (Amershi et al.)

target_raw: Red Hat Kubernetes ML pipeline / role overlap (Benton)

target_raw: Naturalness of buggy code / n-gram language models (Ray, Hellendoorn, ... Devanbu)

target_raw: ExReDiv (Cui et al.)

target_raw: MOOSE (Cui et al.)
evidence: MOOSE [6]: This is a multi-objective crowd worker recommendation, which can maximize the coverage of test requirement, maximize the test experience of the selected crowd workers, and minimize the cost.

target_raw: Cocoon (Xie et al.)

target_canonical: STRING test case prioritization (Ledru et al.)
target_raw: STRING test case prioritization (Ledru et al.)

target_canonical: TOPIC test case prioritization (Thomas et al.)
target_raw: TOPIC test case prioritization (Thomas et al.)

target_raw: NSGA-II (Deb et al.)

target_raw: Bug Detection Rate at k (BDR@k) metric (Cui/Xie et al.)

target_raw: Longitudinal (chronological fold) data setup (Bhattacharya & Neamtiu; Tamrawi et al.)

target_raw: HV, IGD, GS quality indicators (Wang, Ali, Yue et al.)

target_raw: Binary solution encoding and standard genetic operators (Wang, Ali, Yue et al.)

ref: [24] S. Wang, S. Ali, T. Yue, Y. Li, M. Liaaen, ICSE'16, pp. 631-642.

target_raw: GA parameter settings: population 200, 20,000 evaluations (Holland)

target_raw: Mann-Whitney U test (Witten & Frank)

target_canonical: Precision/Recall/F-measure and Information Gain feature ranking (Witten & Frank)
target_raw: Precision/Recall/F-measure and Information Gain feature ranking (Witten & Frank)

ref: [52] I. H. Witten, E. Frank, Data Mining: Practical machine learning tools and techniques. Morgan Kaufmann, 2005.

target_raw: Recent-activity-predicts-future-behavior finding (Zhou & Mockus)
evidence: previous work demonstrated the open source developer's recent activity has greater indicative effect on his future behavior than the activity happened long before [38], [39]. Therefore, we further take the timerelated factors

target_canonical: Learned bug-revealing probability as selection criterion (Chen et al. ICSE'17)
target_raw: Learned bug-revealing probability as selection criterion (Chen et al. ICSE'17)

target_raw: Cold-start problem / recall limits in recommender systems (Ricci et al.)

target_canonical: Elbaum et al.: goal is most bugs for least resources, not all bugs
target_raw: Elbaum et al.: goal is most bugs for least resources, not all bugs
